benignē

adverb

Here benignē is a polite refusal.

Other words

  • Bene vocās, tam grātia est. — kind of you to invite me, but no thank you

    bene vocās, “you invite kindly”; tam grātia est, “I am just as grateful (as if I accepted)” · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 2.3.36: bene vocās: tam grātia est (Lewis & Short s.v. tam); Traupman 104: it was nice of you to invite me, but no, thank you, bene vocās, sed tam grātia est; Traupman 104: no, thanks, tam grātia est; benignē; Traupman 393

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short explains tam grātia est as “I do not accept, but I thank you as much as if I did”. On its own, benignē declines in the same way.

  • Rēctē. — no, thank you; I’m all right

    also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 2.3.33; Ter. Hec. 3.2.20 (Lewis & Short s.v. regō); Traupman 250

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: like benignē, “in politely declining an offer, nothing is wanting, no I thank you”.

Examples

  • Vēscere, sōdēs. — Jam satis est. — At tū, quantum vīs, tolle. — Benignē.

    Eat, please. — I’ve had enough. — Take as much as you like. — No, thank youHor. Epist. I 7, 15–16

  • Īte domum saturae, venit Hesperus.

    Go home full, the evening star is coming (said after the meal)Verg. Ecl. 10, 77

See also be hungry.
